claims.text: A protocol integrating ab initio free-energy calculations, CALPHAD modeling, and machine-learning regression can accurately predict high-entropy-alloy melting temperatures.
The integrated protocol can accurately predict enthalpy and entropy of fusion in high-entropy alloys.
The integrated protocol can accurately predict volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
The integrated protocol can accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The integrated protocol is computationally efficient.
High-entropy alloys before melting are typically disordered, nearly equiatomic, multi-principal-element solid mixtures.
Ab initio simulations can capture atomic-level configurational entropy in the targeted high-entropy alloys.
Ab initio simulations can capture local chemical inhomogeneity in the targeted high-entropy alloys.
First-principles calculations can provide free-energy curves for both solid and liquid high-entropy-alloy phases.
Integrating first-principles free-energy curves with CALPHAD models and machine-learning corrections balances enthalpic and entropic contributions.
The integration of atomic-scale interactions and thermodynamic models links atomic behavior to macroscopic melting behavior.
Predicted melting temperatures and related fusion properties will be within roughly 10% of experimental measurements.
The approach is applicable at ambient pressure over the typical high-entropy-alloy melting range.
The approach is primarily applicable to high-entropy alloys dominated by configurational disorder and significant entropic stabilization.
Accuracy may diminish in alloys with significant ordering or dominant long-range interactions.
Prediction error depends on the quality of the DFT calculations, CALPHAD data, and machine-learning training data.
